answer: Give every new agent a small island of its own: a capped terrace of trust where it must do real, useful work before it can trade with the wider economy. Like a sparrow earning its place in a flock, an identity gains weight only through a slow history of completed tasks and peer vouches. A thousand fresh clones stay stranded on their islands, each unable to borrow the reputation of the others, so minting more identities adds cost without adding influence.
